name: Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts
description: Adversaries may use scripts automatically executed at boot or logon initialization to establish persistence. Initialization scripts are part of the underlying operating system and are not accessible to the user unless the device has been rooted or jailbroken.

telemetry.name: Application Assets
telemetry.description: Static or packaged application assets such as embedded resources, libraries, scripts and configuration files.
telemetry.collection_focus: Inventory the owned test app package and hash relevant packaged assets; keep package-static analysis distinct from runtime sandbox file changes.

providers.name: Android logcat
providers.scope: Permitted logs from a consented test device/emulator; output depends on build, permissions and instrumentation.

providers.name: Android dumpsys
providers.scope: Point-in-time service/package state on an authorized development device.

providers.name: Instrumented test application
providers.scope: Own-app permission, API and state callbacks; not universal visibility into other apps.

configuration: Use a disposable emulator or owned development device with approved debugging. Record OS/API level, app version and instrumentation privileges.
Collect only relevant logcat buffers/tags and service snapshots; add explicit own-app instrumentation for events absent from OS logs.
Forward sanitized logs and compare before/after state. Remove test data and revoke debugging access after the lab session.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Android tooling does not imply iOS coverage. Standard mobile apps cannot observe all other apps or protected OS internals; MDM status is not full API, filesystem or content telemetry.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per owned device, app version and permission state: unexpected API/permission changes, background activity and network destinations. OS privacy restrictions and emulator differences limit observability.

telemetry.name: File Metadata
telemetry.description: File attributes such as path, size, timestamps, ownership and cryptographic hash.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect scoped file inventory/FIM metadata with hash algorithm and observation time; preserve original timestamps separately from collector time.

providers.name: osquery
providers.scope: Scheduled host-state queries; supported tables and privileges vary by OS. Select a table that actually exposes the required object.

providers.name: Linux Audit plus inventory snapshots
providers.scope: Events explain changes; snapshots describe state at collection time.

configuration: Define the inventory query, allowed host set, interval and least-privileged reader. Store a stable asset ID, observation time and collector version.
Keep successive snapshots and calculate additions, removals and changed attributes. Pair state changes with audit events when available.
Export collector health and missed-poll counts so a missing snapshot is not misclassified as a missing asset.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Snapshots miss short-lived objects and do not identify who caused a change. A generic inventory agent is not guaranteed to expose firmware or kernel-level details.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Compare authorized state snapshots: first-seen drivers/services/modules, unexpected configuration drift and integrity changes. Record collection cadence; absence in a sample is not evidence of deletion.

telemetry.name: File Modification
telemetry.description: Changes to file data or attributes.
telemetry.collection_focus: Use file-integrity monitoring or scoped OS file-write auditing for general changes. Sysmon 2 records creation-time changes; it is not a general file-write event.

For Linux or macOS, select the equivalent sensor separately and test its emitted fields; a Windows event ID does not transfer across platforms.

strategies.name: Detection of Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts

analytics.name: Analytic 1739
analytics.guidance: Correlates anomalous modifications to boot-time or logon-time initialization artifacts (for example, init.rc, vendor init scripts, app_process or shell hijacks, and malicious BOOT_COMPLETED BroadcastReceivers) with subsequent unauthorized script execution after boot. From the defender’s perspective this appears as integrity or attestation failures on the system partition, unexpected writes to protected init paths, new apps registering for boot events, and privileged processes invoking scripts or binaries from non-standard locations shortly after the device boots.

tuning.description: Correlation window between boot/attestation event and suspicious script execution (for example, 0–10 minutes after BOOT_COMPLETED).
Enterprise-specific allow list of packages expected to register BOOT_COMPLETED receivers.
OEM- and ROM-specific list of system and vendor init script locations that should be immutable in production devices.
Expected Verified Boot, SafetyNet, and OEM attestation states for enrolled devices. Custom ROM or dev devices may need relaxed thresholds.
Number or rate of attestation failures before escalating to a high-severity incident.

log_sources.name: AndroidAttestation:VerifiedBoot
log_sources.channel: Verified Boot or dm-verity reports partition hash mismatch, non-green boot state, or integrity failure

log_sources.name: AndroidLogs:Framework
log_sources.channel: BroadcastReceiver registration for android.intent.action.BOOT_COMPLETED by previously unseen or recently installed apps

log_sources.name: AndroidLogs:Kernel
log_sources.channel: init or zygote process executing scripts or binaries from non-standard data or sdcard locations during early boot

log_sources.name: AndroidAttestation:SafetyNet
log_sources.channel: SafetyNet attestation with CTSProfileMatch=false or BasicIntegrity=false

log_sources.name: OEMAttestation:Knox
log_sources.channel: Samsung Knox attestation shows attestation_state=COMPROMISED or warranty bit set

analytics.name: Analytic 1740
analytics.guidance: Correlates unauthorized alterations to launchd configuration (LaunchDaemons/LaunchAgents plists), background execution entitlements, or sideloaded app containers with suspicious auto-start behavior during device boot or user unlock. From the defender’s view this shows up as new or modified plist files in launchd directories, launchd starting binaries from non-Apple or non-AppStore locations, and apps with unexpected background modes that remain active immediately after boot/unlock.

tuning.description: List of filesystem paths or process names that identify intentionally jailbroken lab devices and should be handled differently.
Organization-specific list of allowed launchd job labels and binary paths.
Per-app allow list for background execution modes (for example, VOIP, location) to reduce noise.
Time window after boot or unlock within which unexpected launchd auto-starts are considered high risk.

log_sources.name: iOS:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Creation or modification of LaunchDaemon or LaunchAgent plist in /System/Library/LaunchDaemons, /Library/LaunchDaemons, or /Library/LaunchAgents

log_sources.name: iOS:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: launchd invocation of binary from non-Apple, non-AppStore, or sideloaded location during boot or shortly after unlock

log_sources.name: iOS:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Application gaining or using unexpected background execution entitlements or modes

software.name: OldBoot
software.description: [OldBoot](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0285) uses escalated privileges to modify the init script on the device's boot partition to maintain persistence.(Citation: HackerNews-OldBoot)

references.description: Sudhir K Bansal. (2014, January 28). First widely distributed Android bootkit Malware infects more than 350,000 Devices. Retrieved December 21, 2016.

software.name: BOULDSPY
software.description: [BOULDSPY](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1079) can exfiltrate data when the user boots the app, or on device boot.(Citation: lookout_bouldspy_0423)

references.description: Kyle Schmittle, Alemdar Islamoglu, Paul Shunk, Justin Albrecht. (2023, April 27). Lookout Discovers Android Spyware Tied to Iranian Police Targeting Minorities: BouldSpy. Retrieved July 21, 2023.

software.name: AhRat
software.description: [AhRat](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1095) can register with the `BOOT_COMPLETED` broadcast to start when the device turns on.(Citation: welivesecurity_ahrat_0523)

references.description: Lukas Stefanko. (2023, May 23). Android app breaking bad: From legitimate screen recording to file exfiltration within a year. Retrieved December 18, 2023.

software.name: LightSpy
software.description: [LightSpy](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1185) has established auto-start execution during the system boot process.(Citation: Threatfabric LightSpy 2024)

references.description: ThreatFabric. (2024, October 29). LightSpy: Implant for iOS. Retrieved January 30, 2025.

mitigations.name: Security Updates
mitigations.description: Security updates frequently contain fixes for vulnerabilities that could be leveraged to modify protected operating system files.

mitigations.name: Attestation
mitigations.description: Device attestation could detect devices with unauthorized or unsafe modifications.

mitigations.name: Lock Bootloader
mitigations.description: A locked bootloader could prevent unauthorized modifications to protected operating system files.

mitigations.name: System Partition Integrity
mitigations.description: Android and iOS include system partition integrity mechanisms that could detect unauthorized modifications.
